event: Confirmed by code reading: the mask cuts the value, so a USER of 0xDEADBEEF wouldn't match.

I verified the finding: the k24 check in `cptra_smoke_test_mcu_mbox_target_user.c` can't detect MBOX USER taking the written value.

At line 188 the test compares the USER read-back to `0xDEADBEEF & MCU_MBOX0_CSR_MBOX_CMD_STATUS_STATUS_MASK`. That cuts the value down to a few low bits, so a USER that really became `0xDEADBEEF` would not equal it and the test would still pass. The line looks copied from the CMD_STATUS check at line 176.

I did not find where `MCU_MBOX0_CSR_MBOX_CMD_STATUS_STATUS_MASK` is defined, so I haven't confirmed its exact value. The conclusion holds for any mask narrower than 32 bits.

I didn't change any files. The verdict was accepted on the second submission, after the first attempt failed because the tool wasn't available under that name.
